title: Author + socialize PRD for workload-aware batching defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient tiers)
creator: Aditya Rao
description:
## Context
We are shipping “workload-aware batching defaults”: recommended batching profiles mapped to 3 customer-facing latency SLO tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient). The intent is to reduce $/1K tokens and improve throughput without introducing unpredictable tail latency or overload behavior.

This ticket exists to:
1) Author and socialize the PRD
2) Align on launch criteria + go/no-go gates
3) Coordinate cross-team dependencies (Runtime, SRE/Obs, Hosted API, Dedicated, Console, Docs)

Primary engineering owner: Serving Runtime (Sofia Ivanova / Lena Fischer)
SRE lead: Sean Gallagher
Hosted API PM sponsor: Nikhil Sharma
Dedicated PM sponsor: Lauren Bishop

## PRD doc link
Confluence: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-batching-profiles-slo-tiers.json
(If you’re reading this in Linear: see “Batching Profiles — SLO Tiers” under Product Docs → Requirements.)

## Problem statement
Batching settings today are a foot-gun:
- Customers (and internal teams) can accidentally pick aggressive batching that looks fine at p50 but blows up p99 under mixed workloads.
- The “right” knob set is workload-dependent (prompt-length distribution, streaming vs non-streaming, concurrency) and hardware/model-dependent.
- Our current guidance is fragmented (runtime docs, forum answers, support playbooks) and not easily explainable in Console.

We need defaults that are safe, explainable, and easy to override, with observability that makes it obvious when the system is in a degraded/overload mode.

## Goals / success criteria
### Product goals
- Customers can select an SLO tier (fast/standard/cost-efficient) at route/model policy level and get predictable behavior.
- If customers do nothing, they get a sane default tier (see “Default behavior” below) with no breaking change to correctness.
- Dedicated customers can override tier + specific knobs with clear precedence rules.

### Business + performance goals (measured)
- Improve throughput and reduce $/1K tokens for typical Hosted API traffic without increasing incident rate.
- Publish tier-level expectations and “why this profile” explanations (Console + docs) without over-promising.

### Reliability goals
- Preserve correctness under mixed workloads and avoid starvation.
- Under overload, behavior must be predictable and reversible (backpressure/load shedding/kill switch).

## Non-goals (initial release)
- Real-time per-tenant auto-tuning (we will do recommendations + heuristic selection, not continuous auto-optimization).
- Changes to cross-region routing beyond existing smart routing policies.

## Users / personas
1) Hosted API builder (PLG): wants a simple knob to bias latency vs cost.
2) Enterprise operator (Dedicated): wants predictable behavior + ability to override and audit the effective profile.
3) SRE/on-call: needs dashboards/alerts with clear abort criteria and reason codes.
4) Support/CS: needs a deterministic troubleshooting flow (“try standard → fast” is not enough; we need signals).

## Customer-facing tiers (definition intent)
Note: numeric targets live in SLO tier spec owned by SRE. This PRD defines product semantics + behavior expectations.
- Fast: prioritize tail latency (p99) and streaming responsiveness; tighter wait budget; more conservative batching; stronger admission control.
- Standard: balanced; default for most customers; moderate batching with guardrails.
- Cost-efficient: prioritize throughput/$; allow larger batches and more queueing within reason; must still have overload safeguards.

## Default behavior
- Hosted API: default tier = Standard unless an endpoint is explicitly tagged “realtime/interactive” by Redwood (initially: chat+streaming routes), in which case default tier = Fast.
- Dedicated: default tier = Standard unless tenant policy sets otherwise. Dedicated customers can set an account-level default tier.
- Private: follow same config semantics; defaults depend on deployment templates but should match Hosted/Dedicated behavior.

## Requirements
### Config + policy (Platform)
- Tier selection must be configurable at route/model policy level.
- Override precedence must be explicit and testable:
  1) Customer override (Dedicated tenant / Private deployment)
  2) Route policy
  3) Tier default profile
  4) Model/hardware constraints (may clamp effective knobs)
  5) Overload mode (temporary behavior change)
- Backwards compatibility: existing manual batching config should continue to work, with a deprecation/migration story.

### Runtime scheduler behavior (Runtime)
- Workload-aware heuristics can incorporate at minimum:
  - streaming vs non-streaming
  - prompt-length buckets
  - concurrency/queue depth signals
- Must avoid starvation under mixed prompt lengths; fast tier must not get stuck behind cost-efficient workloads.
- Must provide clear “reason codes” for profile selection and any clamping/overload behavior.

### Observability (SRE/Obs)
- Metrics must be segmented by tier (with cardinality controls):
  - latency p50/p95/p99 (prefill, decode, end-to-end)
  - batch size distribution, queue depth, wait times
  - admission control / shed rate
  - cache hit rate (where relevant)
  - cost attribution proxies ($/token, tokens/sec)
- Dashboards must support:
  - rollout monitoring by cohort (feature flag)
  - regression detection vs baseline
- Alerting must distinguish paging vs ticketing; fast-tier p99 regressions should page only when correlated with elevated error rate or sustained over-threshold.

### Console + Docs
- Console must show:
  - current effective tier
  - whether it’s default vs override
  - “why this profile” explanation (reason codes summarized in human language)
- Docs must include:
  - what each tier optimizes for
  - how to choose tiers (examples: chat streaming vs batch summarization)
  - how to override / opt out
  - troubleshooting checklist (what metrics to check before switching tiers)

## Launch plan (staged)
1) Internal canary (runtime + perf suite gates)
2) Hosted API subset (feature-flagged by project/route; exclude high-risk regions initially)
3) Dedicated opt-in (account-level flag + Console surfacing)
4) Broader default enablement (Hosted) once SLO + error budget gates are green for 2+ weeks

Kill switch requirements:
- Global disable
- Per-tier disable (fallback to Standard) if a tier is problematic
- Per-route override to pin old behavior during incident response

## Launch criteria (go/no-go)
### Must be green
- Perf canary gates passing for top model families and top regions per tier thresholds.
- No sustained SLO regression vs baseline for standard tier in control cohort.
- Error budget impact within agreed limits (per SRE analysis) during canary.
- Telemetry costs remain bounded (tier labels + reason codes do not blow up cardinality).
- Docs merged + support playbook updated.

### Must be ready
- Clear rollback steps documented and tested in a canary environment.
- Support has an internal FAQ and a triage flow.

## Open questions (resolved in PRD review)
- Tier naming: “fast / standard / cost-efficient” chosen (avoid “realtime” implying guaranteed realtime; align with messaging guidance).
- Default tier for streaming: fast by default for Redwood-tagged interactive streaming endpoints; otherwise standard.
- How to message “cost-efficient”: emphasize throughput/$ improvements; do not promise specific % savings; publish benchmark ranges with caveats.

## Coordination checklist
- [x] PRD drafted and shared with Runtime (Sofia/Lena), SRE (Sean), Hosted API PM (Nikhil), Dedicated PM (Lauren)
- [x] Align on tier semantics and default behavior
- [x] Define launch criteria + go/no-go gates with SRE/Runtime
- [x] Ensure docs/console workstreams have owners + timelines
- [x] Confirm feature flag + kill switch requirements with Release Eng

## Reference threads / artifacts
- SLO tier definitions: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/latency-slo-tiers-definition-fast-standard-cost-efficient.json
- Design doc (runtime): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/workload-aware-batching-defaults-design.json
- Dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/batching-defaults-observability-dashboard-spec.json
- Console spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-ui-batching-recommendations.json
- Docs plan: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/public-docs-plan-batching-defaults.json

## Notes for reviewers
This PRD is intentionally opinionated about defaults + messaging. The runtime can evolve heuristics, but the customer contract (tier semantics, overrides, observability, and rollout safety) should remain stable.
comments: 2025-12-05 (Aditya Rao): Initial PRD outline posted. Need SRE to confirm we can publish tier targets (or at least “intent + typical ranges”).

2025-12-09 (Sean Gallagher): Please separate “published tier targets” from “internal gating thresholds.” Suggest we publish tier intent + streaming guidance; keep hard p99 numbers in the SLO doc (internal) until we validate in canary across regions.

2025-12-11 (Sofia Ivanova): Runtime can support tier selection + reason codes, but we need to be explicit about precedence and clamping due to model constraints. Please include in PRD so Support doesn’t treat clamping as a bug.

2025-12-16 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated requirement: tenant override must win over route policy; also need ability to lock a tenant to Standard during an incident. Please include a “tenant pin” example in docs.

2026-01-07 (Nikhil Sharma): Hosted API default proposal accepted: Standard by default; Fast by default only for Redwood-tagged interactive streaming routes. Avoid making “fast” the universal default; it would cost too much at scale.

2026-01-15 (Allison Grant): Observability concern: tier labels + reason codes can explode cardinality. PRD updated to require cardinality controls and sampling guidance; will review taxonomy before rollout.

2026-02-20 (Aditya Rao): PRD finalized and moved to ‘Approved’ in Confluence. Launch criteria section updated with explicit must-be-green list. Next action: track execution via ENG/DES tickets and runtime-1.22 launch brief.
